dissents.topic: Severity of the coerceNumber null→0 substitution

positions.position: P0 — semantic change disguised as typing refactor; commit message lies about runtime behavior
P0 — defensive-as-substitute-for-correctness; contradicts PR's no-behavior-change claim
P1 — quiet semantic change concealed under a type adapter; the 0 fallback is load-bearing and arbitrary
P1 — complects 'not a number' with 'zero' into one return value
P1 — LSP-style postcondition weakening; same signature, weaker postcondition
P1 — behavior change masquerading as typing refactor; data shape lied about at boundary

dissents.topic: Severity of the smuggled empty-domain throw / behavior change vs. PR description

positions.position: P0 — must be split into separate patches (types vs. empty-domain throw vs. coerceNumber swap); commit message is wrong about what the commit does
P2 — real behavior change but probably the right one; should be called out, not folded into a typing PR
P2 — almost certainly the right change but deserves explicit mention in changelog as breaking
P1 (related): the throw itself is fine, but it is implemented via a smuggled-goto error() call without explicit throw/return

dissents.topic: Is the public API actually 'typesafe'? Should domain be NonEmptyArray<number>?

positions.position: P1 — 'typesafe' claim is false; public API still accepts number[]. Precondition is also wrong: needs length >= 2, not >= 1, because single-element domains produce degenerate [x,x]
P1 — either make the public type NonEmptyArray<number> or drop the runtime throw; half-typing is the worst of both
P1 — SPEC-MISSING; type system was just upgraded, this is the moment to encode the precondition in the type
P1 — complects 'I accept any array' with 'but I will reject most of them'; should be NonEmptyArray at the boundary
P2 — current shape pays for types and still does a runtime check; not the typesafe refactor the PR title advertises
P2 — wrong data structure at the boundary; tightening the input would make helpers shrink to obvious arithmetic

dissents.topic: Is the single-element degenerate-domain case a real bug?

positions.position: P0 — precondition should be length >= 2; isNonEmpty admits [5] which produces silently degenerate [5,5]
Did not flag — implicitly accept length >= 1 as the precondition

issues.description: coerceNumber silently substitutes 0 for null/NaN, changing observable behavior of panLinear/zoomLinear despite PR claiming no behavior change
issues.detail: The old code used identity/toNumber so non-numeric domain entries propagated as NaN (a loud, diagnosable signal). The new coerceNumber: x => toNumber(x) ?? 0 quietly converts null/undefined/unparsable values to 0. This is a real semantic change disguised as a type adapter, and the PR description's claim of 'same runtime behavior as before' is false. The comment even brags 'Unlike toNumber, coerceNumber always returns a number' — papering over a type mismatch with a runtime lie to make the compiler happy.

issues.description: Behavior change smuggled into a 'just adding types' patch — pan/zoom now throw on empty domain where they previously returned [NaN, NaN]
issues.detail: The new isNonEmpty guards call error() on empty domains; previously the functions returned silently degenerate values. The PR description says 'Everything else should have same runtime behavior as before, I just added types' which is contradicted by the diff. Torvalds calls for splitting into THREE-PATCHES (types, empty-domain throw, coerceNumber swap), each with its own justification. Hickey/Liskov agree it is probably the right change but must be named as a breaking change, not folded into a typing PR.

issues.description: Precondition is incomplete: isNonEmpty admits single-element domains that silently produce degenerate [x,x] results
issues.detail: The functions read both domain[0] and peek(domain), so the real precondition is length >= 2, not length >= 1. A single-element domain [5] passes isNonEmpty, then d0 == d1, dd == 0, and pan returns [5, 5] — a silently degenerate output. The author has stated half the precondition and called it done.

issues.description: Public API declares domain as number[] but the contract is non-empty (and arguably length >= 2) — 'typesafe' refactor still relies on runtime checks
issues.detail: Exported functions accept domain: number[] and then runtime-check isNonEmpty. NonEmptyArray<T> is already defined in the file and peek has a matching overload, so the precondition should be encoded in the public type (NonEmptyArray<number> or [number, number, ...number[]]). As-is, callers get nothing from the type system, the runtime guard is pure overhead, and the title's 'typesafe' claim is aspirational. Either make the public type honest or drop the runtime guard — picking both is half-typing.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog/panPow/zoomPow read domain[0] before the helper's empty-domain guard runs
issues.detail: Math.sign(domain[0]) and similar expressions are computed in the public entry points before delegating to pan/zoom, so on an empty domain they evaluate Math.sign(undefined) = NaN and only then hit the helper's throw. The error happens by accident of evaluation order, not by design. Hoist the isNonEmpty check to the public entry points, or accept NonEmptyArray<number> at the boundary so internal helpers can trust the invariant.

issues.description: Control-flow smuggled goto: error() called without explicit throw/return; termination depends on imported helper's side effect
issues.detail: The guard reads 'if (!isNonEmpty(domain)) error(...)' with no throw, no return, no explicit control transfer. Termination depends on error() throwing as a side effect, invisible at the call site. If error() were ever changed to log-and-return, execution would fall through to domain[0] on an empty array. Fix is trivial: 'throw error(...)' or restructure so the throwing contract is visible.

issues.description: Local identity rebinding shadows the shared accessors.identity instead of fixing the type at the source
issues.detail: The original imported identity from ./accessors.js. The new file drops that import and defines a local const identity: TransformFn = x => x. Either accessors.identity has the wrong type signature (fix it there, where every caller benefits) or this is a gratuitous local copy that will drift. Forking the codebase's identity function inside one module because the types didn't line up is incidental complexity introduced by the types, not the problem.

issues.description: Return type Domain = [number, number] hides that results can legitimately be [NaN, NaN] or [Infinity, ...]
issues.detail: panLog/zoomLog/panPow/zoomPow compose log and pow with arbitrary numeric input; log of a non-positive number is NaN, pow of negative bases with fractional exponents is NaN. The Domain alias asserts 'a pair of numbers' but the value model is really 'a pair of possibly-degenerate numbers'. The new types make the call sites feel safe without making the values safe.

issues.description: peek overload promises non-undefined return but implementation cannot enforce it for caller-claimed non-empty arrays
issues.detail: The new overload peek<T>(array: readonly [T, ...T[]]): T promises a non-undefined return, but array[array.length - 1] returns T | undefined at runtime if T includes undefined or if a caller passes a sparse array typed as non-empty. The overload narrows the postcondition based on a structural type the runtime cannot verify. Acceptable in practice but the spec should note that peek trusts its caller's claim of non-emptiness.

issues.description: peek narrowing may not flow through to the d1 binding inside pan/zoom
issues.detail: After isNonEmpty(domain) narrows the type, peek(domain) should pick up the non-undefined overload. But peek is called with the parameter binding; TS may not re-narrow. If not, d1 is silently number | undefined and arithmetic on it is only well-typed by coincidence. Add an assertion or restructure so the narrowing is visible to the reader.

issues.description: peek's second overload is redundant with the implementation signature
issues.detail: The two declared overloads plus the implementation signature work, but the second overload peek<T>(array: readonly T[]): T | undefined duplicates the implementation signature exactly. TypeScript allows it; it is still noise. One overload + the impl would be enough.

issues.description: isNonEmpty type guard buys a runtime check but no compile-time leverage at the call sites
issues.detail: isNonEmpty narrows domain to NonEmptyArray<T>, but the following lines read domain[0] and peek(domain) without exploiting the narrowing. Either pass the narrowed array into peek so the non-undefined overload fires, or drop the type guard and just write 'if (domain.length === 0) error(...)'. Right now it is ceremony around a length check.

issues.description: Precondition duplicated across pan and zoom helpers instead of enforced once at the boundary
issues.detail: Two copies of isNonEmpty(domain) || error(...) sit in pan() and zoom(). Two copies of the same precondition is two opportunities for contracts to drift. If domain were typed NonEmptyArray<number> at the helper level, the check would be needed only at the public-API boundary and the type system would discharge the rest.

issues.description: Test coverage for the new throw covers only panLinear and zoomLinear, not the log/pow/symlog variants
issues.detail: Two of eight exported functions exercise the new throw. The other six share the same code path through pan/zoom, so the gap is small in practice — but if the check ever moves during a later refactor, only the linear variants are guarded by tests. Either add a parametric test that loops the eight exports over [], or note explicitly that the helper-level check covers them. Tests also do not cover single-element degenerate case nor the null-in-domain behavior change introduced by coerceNumber.

issues.description: Behavioral change in error path is undocumented in PR description / changelog
issues.detail: The PR says 'Everything else should have same runtime behavior as before, I just added types' but introduces a new throw on empty domain (previously these returned [NaN, NaN] silently). That is a real, observable behavior change for any caller that passed [] and depended on the non-throwing path. It deserves explicit mention in the changelog so downstream consumers see it as a breaking change.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog still depend on Math.sign(domain[0]) with no guard for domain[0] === 0
issues.detail: Pre-existing behavior, not introduced by this PR: log(0) is -Infinity and Math.sign(0) is 0, which makes log(sign) return Math.log(0 * x) = -Infinity for all x. The function silently returns a degenerate domain. Not in scope to fix, but the literate comment should at least note the precondition domain[0] !== 0 for the log variants.

issues.description: Domain alias is tight on outputs but inputs remain loose (number[], Anchor)
issues.detail: The return type Domain = [number, number] is the right data-structure-first move — it says what the function produces. The asymmetry is that inputs are loose while outputs are tight. Tightening the input side would make the helpers shrink to obvious arithmetic with no guards. Also worth a deliberate sweep of downstream consumers in vega-scale that may have treated the return as number[].

synthesis.summary: The panel converges strongly on two structural problems and one taxonomic one. Structurally: (1) coerceNumber silently substitutes 0 for null/NaN — all six reviewers flagged this, with Torvalds and Dijkstra calling it P0 and the rest P1, because it is a real semantic change in panLinear/zoomLinear that directly contradicts the PR's 'same runtime behavior as before' claim; (2) the public API declares domain: number[] and then runtime-checks non-emptiness, when NonEmptyArray<number> is already defined in the same file — five of six reviewers say this is the actual typesafe refactor the PR title advertises, and Dijkstra goes further to point out the real precondition is length >= 2, not >= 1, because single-element domains produce silently degenerate [x,x] output (a P0 he alone caught). Taxonomically: Torvalds wants the PR split into three patches (types, empty-domain throw, coerceNumber swap); Hickey and Liskov agree the empty-domain throw is probably correct but must be called out as a breaking change rather than smuggled in. The strongest preserved disagreement is on severity of the coerceNumber change (Torvalds/Dijkstra P0 vs the other four P1) and on whether the single-element degenerate case is a real bug (Dijkstra P0, no one else flagged it). Minor findings — local identity shadowing, peek overload redundancy, smuggled-goto via error() without throw, thin test coverage of log/pow/symlog variants — are broadly agreed at P1/P2.
